In [[algebraic geometry]], '''Sumihiro's theorem''', introduced by {{harv|Sumihiro|1974}}, states that a [[normal variety|normal algebraic variety]] with an [[Group action (mathematics)|action]] of a [[Maximal torus|torus]] can be [[Cover (topology)|covered]] by torus-invariant affine open subsets.

The "normality" in the hypothesis cannot be relaxed.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Cox |first1=David A. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=AoSDAwAAQBAJ&pg=PA151 |title=Toric Varieties |last2=Little |first2=John B. |last3=Schenck |first3=Henry K. |author-link=David A. Cox |author-link2=John B. Little (mathematician) |author-link3=Hal Schenck |date=2011 |publisher=American Mathematical Soc. |isbn=978-0-8218-4819-7 |language=en}}</ref> The hypothesis that the group acting on the variety is a torus can also not be relaxed.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bialynicki-Birula decomposition of a non-singular quasi-projective scheme. |url=https://mathoverflow.net/questions/94620/bialynicki-birula-decomposition-of-a-non-singular-quasi-projective-scheme |access-date=2023-03-10 |website=MathOverflow |language=en}}</ref>
